turns.text: The previous story examined Kernel PCA. Now the camera turns to NMF and a new question along the same timeline: If we take NMF apart, which idea truly changed the direction of research?

Daniel Lee and H. Sebastian Seung showed that non-negative matrix factorization can learn additive parts of faces and semantic features of text. The constraint that factors remain nonnegative encouraged interpretable parts-based representations.
That sounds like a promising direction. What mechanism actually makes it work?
A data matrix is approximated as nonnegative basis parts multiplied by nonnegative activations.

Experts generally treat NMF as a foundational method for interpretable latent factors. Its long-term legacy is the parts-based view that influenced topic modeling, source separation, recommender systems, and explainable representation learning.
Seen alongside Kernel PCA, NMF reveals how the same technical question can echo across different eras.
